stem: A label press prints 45 sheets each minute, each sheet yields 16 labels, and finished labels are packed 500 to a box. How many boxes can be filled completely from the labels the press produces in 4 hours of continuous printing?
subject: MATH

stem: A gable bracket has the shape of triangle \(RST\), in which the side \(RS\) is the same length as the side \(RT\). When the side \(ST\) is extended beyond T, the angle it makes with the side \(TR\) measures 118°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the angle at R?
subject: MATH

stem: A grain hopper is a cylinder of radius 3 metres and height 5 metres with a cone of the same radius and height 4 metres joined to its base. What is the total volume of the hopper, in cubic metres?
subject: MATH

stem: A drawing office sets out a right triangle \(JKL\) in which the right angle is at L, so the angles at J and at K have measures that add to 90°. The office records \(\tan J=\frac{3}{4}\). What is the value of \(\cos K\)?
subject: MATH

stem: A caterer packs portions into trays that hold 8 portions each and boxes that hold 5 portions each. She must pack at least 60 portions and may use at most 9 containers in all. If she uses exactly 4 boxes, how many trays must she use?
subject: MATH

stem: The mass of a spool of cable is a linear function of the length of cable wound on it. A spool holding 40 metres of cable has a mass of 27 kilograms, and a spool holding 100 metres of cable has a mass of 51 kilograms. What is the mass, in kilograms, of the empty spool?
subject: MATH

stem: In a chemistry stockroom, 2 crates and 5 drums together weigh 197 kilograms, and 4 crates and 3 drums together weigh 219 kilograms. What is the combined weight, in kilograms, of one crate and one drum?
subject: MATH

stem: A conical pile of road salt has a radius of 9 metres and a height of 4 metres. The salt is reshaped, with none lost, into a cylinder of radius 6 metres. What is the height, in metres, of the cylinder?
subject: MATH
